read_me: The directory of foreign universities that `app/seed/study_abroad.py` loads.
Every row here carries only what does not change: a real institution's name, the
country it is in, its city, whether the state funds it, and its own domain. Nothing
else is seeded, because nothing else can be checked from here.
Tuition, intake months, application deadlines and English-test requirements are
deliberately absent. They move every year, and a number that looks like a fact is the
one thing a family will budget against. An unseeded field renders as
'Not verified yet - check the university's own site', which is the honest state and
the reason this file can be shipped without a single fee in it.
To fill a row in, open the university's own admissions page, read the figure, then
add these keys to that object:
"tuition_note": "what the fee actually is, in the currency it is charged in",
"intakes": ["September 2027", "January 2027"],
"application_urls": {"graduate": "https://..."},
"english_test_note": "...",
"deadline_note": "...",
"source_url": "the exact page you read it on",
and set "verified": true. Without source_url and verified_at the page keeps saying
it has not been checked, which is what the seed script insists on.
Every row lives in one of the six destinations the database describes: united-states,
united-kingdom, canada, germany, australia, ireland. A row naming any other country is
skipped by the loader rather than given an invented destination - add that country to
`app/seed/study_abroad_data.py` first, its visa and intake copy with it, and only then
put its institutions here.
Re-running the seed never overwrites a row somebody has filled in: it only adds
universities whose slug is not in the database yet.
